To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the long-term application (13 years) of GM, WS, RS and FYM to rice–wheat cropping system in Punjab, resulted in significant improvement in soil physical properties, but had no effect on the yield of wheat.

(i) organic amendments increased organic matter content and improved soil physical properties; (ii) organic amendments increased crop yield; (iii) there was no residual effect on wheat yield of organic amendments applied in rice; and (iv) FYM application to the rice crop had a residual effect on wheat.
the addition of green manure and crop straw residues significantly increased organic carbon content, improved soil aggregation and increased soil strength in the rice–watt rotation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sustainability of rice–wheat cropping system and the effect of organic inputs on soil physical properties.
the sustainability of rice–wheat cropping system in India.
the effects of long-term application of organic materials on the physical and hydraulic properties and crop yield in rice–wheat rotations in the Punjab, India.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the long-term effects of the organic treatments were not significant on rice and wheat yields but they improved the physical properties of the soil.

the addition of FYM to rice, followed by incorporation of GM, WS, RS and FYM to wheat in combination, is the best management strategy to improve the physical properties of soil and increase the yield potential of the rice– wheat rotation in Punjab.
GM, WS, RS, FYM and urea alone or in combination can be used to sustain the soil health and crop productivity of rice–wheat systems in Punjab, India.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
application of FYM and GM to rice, and FYM +GM to wheat, in combination with urea, is recommended for sustainable management of rice–wheat cropping system.
the application of organic manures, particularly FYM and GM in the rice–wheatsystem, is beneficial for improving soil properties and rice and wheat yields.

GM and FYM application to the soil in rice–wheat cropping system improved the soil physical properties, and increased the soil OC, which in turn enhanced soil water retention and reduced the bulk density, thereby increasing the infiltration rates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the application of FYM, GM, WS and/or RS to the rice–w Wheat system can improve the physical properties of the soil and maintain soil quality.
application of GM to the rice–wheats system in Punjab is a sustainable practice that not only improves soil properties but also enhances rice yield.
the application of FYM, GM, WS, RS or their combinations to rice–wheat systems is beneficial in maintaining soil physical properties and improving crop yields.
